dod_intent_evidence: SBIR Phase II award from the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency for a flight-prototype electro-optic shutter (own-abstracts section), plus LinkedIn about stating they build for 'the US Government, US and NATO Defense Contractors'.
score_evidence: "pulsed laser systems with durations from 60 fsec to 20 nsec with Pulse Repetition Frequency from <0.1 Hz to more than 200 kHz" → lab_language_intensity (pure spec talk, no operational framing)

"Low SWaP - High Average Power Water Cooled Optical Mount" / "we will develop a fast Electro-optic cell... ruggedization necessary for high-altitude flight" → deployment_awareness_absence (low; they are explicitly fluent in SWaP-C and flight-environment ruggedization)

"the development, production and fielding of some of the most advanced laser and electrical optical systems in the world" → operator_absence (fielding is mentioned but no operator/training/CONOPS language anywhere on the site)
"Junior Electrical/Controls Engineer" (only open role, Blitz live) → hiring_profile_skew (single junior engineering hire, no field/test/integration/compliance role)

"The decision to become a hardware provider resulted in explosive growth that is an on-going challenge for the company" → stage_pressure (small team stretched by growth, single active Phase II with follow-on flight-prototype milestones)

blind_spots.blind_spot: Two Flight Prototype Range-Gate (FPRG) units must meet NGA-212-001's altitude, temperature, and pressure envelope, but Phase II language treats ruggedization as a 'second engineering cycle' still being designed, not a validated capability.
blind_spots.operator_reality: An aircrew depending on this shutter for sensor protection at operational altitude has zero tolerance for a unit that hasn't survived thermal/pressure qualification — 'if sufficient funds and schedule remain' is a valley-of-death tell, not a design footnote.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Small design-and-analysis-turned-hardware shop (15 employees) is still funding qualification testing out of the same Phase II budget meant to deliver flight units.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "a second engineering cycle will produce a EO shutter designed for the temperature range, pressure and ruggedization necessary for high-altitude flight"

blind_spots.blind_spot: The EO Cell and Electric Power and Switching System (EPSS) are described purely as lab hardware deliverables — no mention of who calibrates or realigns the optical assembly once it's mounted on an actual aircraft.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Precision electro-optic shutters drift and need field alignment; without a documented sustainment/spares plan, the unit works in the lab and fails after the first hard landing or maintenance cycle in theater.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company's entire public-facing language (site + SBIR abstract) is written for a program-office/engineering audience, never an end-operator or maintainer audience.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "Two Flight Prototype Range-Gate (FPRG) units will be provided" — with no accompanying discussion of installation, calibration, or field maintenance

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/RMF, CMMC, or ITAR language anywhere despite building sensor-protection hardware that will integrate with government aircraft electronics and control systems.
blind_spots.operator_reality: If the EPSS has any embedded firmware or interfaces with aircraft avionics networks, it needs a cybersecurity accreditation path before installation — silence on this in a company this small is a common cause of late-stage program delay.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company's technical identity is rooted in optics/photonics engineering (15-year design-and-analysis consultancy background), not systems cybersecurity or acquisition compliance.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: (absence) — no ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR term appears anywhere in the ~1082 words of their own language

opener_hook: Your NGA Phase II abstract commits two Flight Prototype Range-Gate units to altitude, temperature, and pressure qualification in the same engineering cycle that's still being designed — what's the plan if flight ruggedization eats the schedule before delivery?
what_they_do: Custom high-speed electro-optic shutters and pulsed-laser hardware for defense sensor-protection and range-gated imaging, transitioning a 15-employee design shop into a flight-hardware supplier.
